scope: Corollary 18.1 of the manuscript “Virtual compact specialness of hyperbolic one-relator groups” (preprints/Virtual-compact-specialness-of-hyperbolic-one-relator-groups-September-25-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 258 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 a6c45541e6943005), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 139. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let G be one of the following groups. 1. A one-relator group G = F(X)/⟨⟨r⟩⟩, where X is finite and r ∈ F(X) is arbitrary, such that either G is word-hyperbolic or G contains no subgroup isomorphic to BS(m, n) for any nonzero integers m, n. 2. A word-hyperbolic ascending mapping torus G = ⟨F, t | t−1 ft = ϕ(f) (f ∈ F)⟩, where F is a free group of finite rank and ϕ : F → F is injective. There are a finite-index subgroup H ≤ G, an integer d ≥ 0, an automorphism α of the rank-d free group Fd, and an embedding H ,→ Fd ⋊α Z. In particular, G is virtually free-by-cyclic: the same H fits into an exact sequence 1 −→ K −→ H −→ Q −→ 1, K free, Q ≤ Z. The rank of K may be infinite, and Q may be trivial.
